newsitem.title: USA: Cap on CRP size stripped from U.S. spending bill.
newsitem.headline: Cap on CRP size stripped from U.S. spending bill.

text.p: The U.S. House deleted language from an emergency spending bill Thursday to limit new enrollments this year in the Conservation Reserve to 14 million acres.
"We finally conquered the problem," said Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith, Oregon Republican.
During floor debate on the bill, Smith challenged the cap as impermissible meddling -- legislating on an appropriations bill -- and won a ruling from the chair to strip the provision from the bill.
The Senate has no cap in its version of the bill.

The cap was written into the House bill by an Appropriations subcommittee to ensure consideration of land in the eastern half of the nation, where maintaining water purity is a concern. The full committee brushed aside an attempt by farm-state lawmakers to erase the cap.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman opposed the cap.
Contracts on 21 million acres of CRP land expire this fall. Farmers offered 25.6 million acres for enrollment during a sign-up in March. USDA has said it might accept up to 19 million acres.
The spending bill also would reduce funding this fiscal year for U.S. agricultural export credit and export subsidy programs.
